The '''Koboks''' were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoids]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Koboth]]. Strong and nimble despite a [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]]-like frame, a Kobok was a formidable opponent in combat due to spikes that projected from each [[Limb/Legends|limb]]; the natural weapons delivered a potent venom capable of knocking out [[Human/Legends|Human]]-sized targets for several [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]]. Each member of the [[Species/Legends|species]] possessed three [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], two at the front of the head and one at the back, which provided a 360-degree field of vision. The fuzzy carapace that covered the face was mutable and allowed a Kobok to convey expressions with the mouth and eyes.

Their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], on the fringe of the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]], was ruled by the [[Koboth Union]], and their control extended over an area known as [[Kobothi Space]]. Although the species brokered trade agreements with neighbors such as the [[Trianii/Legends|Trianii]] and the [[Hiitian/Legends|Hiitians]], they clashed with their neighbors from the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] and warred for [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. The rivalry lead to such conflagrations as the violent [[Mavvan Conflict]], which gave rise to the elite Kobok unit known as the [[Kobothi S-Corps]].

The Koboks became known for their militarism due to such wars, and outside their sphere of influence, the Koboks had a reputation as violent and sneaky. Few representatives of the species migrated to worlds outside Kobothi [[Realspace/Legends|Space]]&mdash;with the exception of the planet [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], which had a sizable Kobok population&mdash;but those who did emigrate tended to work as [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], and [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], and thus reinforced their species' martial reputation.

==Biology and appearance==
===Features===
[[File:Gaff_storybook.jpg|thumb|left|260px|Koboks were tall and slight humanoids.]]
The Koboks were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of thin, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]]<ref name="GATORW" /> [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoids]].<ref name="CSWE 223" /> The Kobok body was roughly [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]], with a bipedal stance and a slight, almost [[Bone/Legends|skeletal]] frame. A typical member of the species stood between 1.3 and 1.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, but due to the body's thinness, rarely weighed more than sixty [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]. Nevertheless, Koboks were quite strong despite the slight frame,<ref name="GATORW" /> and some could jump as high as half their body length.<ref name="TOTRC">{{DroidsCite|Tail of the Roon Comets}}</ref> In general, their constitution was not particularly robust. Nevertheless, they were immune to the more deadly effects of an ailment known as [[Rooze Disease]]&mdash;the medicine for the illness did cause them to laugh uncontrollably, though.<ref name="TFC">{{DroidsCite|The Frozen Citadel}}</ref> A Kobok reached adolescence at age nine, adulthood at age seventeen, and had a life expectancy of seventy-six [[Standard year/Legends|years]].<ref name="GATORW" />

Although yellow Koboks were most common, the [[Color/Legends|coloration]] of a Kobok's carapace depended on the region of the species' [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Koboth]], from which the individual came. For example, the Koboks from the [[Kuurok Peninsula]] tended to sport a dark green to black carapace. Other Koboks had crème, beige,<ref name="GATORW" /> brown,<ref name="EFTMS" /> orange,<ref name="G DB">{{DB|character|gaff|Gaff}}</ref> or green colorations.<ref name="AGTTSWU2" /> The carapace featured several spikes and protrusions, and it was rigid and fairly durable. This covering afforded the Koboks resistance to the harmful effects of exposure to [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]].<ref name="GATORW" />

===Other features===
Claws, also referred to as ''foreclaws''<ref name="GATORW" /> and ''stingers'',<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> grew from each of a Kobok's [[Limb/Legends|limbs]], four on each forearm and three on each shin.<ref name="GATORW" /> Kobok combatants could extend these natural weapons somewhat in preparation for combat<ref name="TRG">{{DroidsCite|The Roon Games}}</ref> to allow for a slashing attack against enemies.<ref name="GATORW" /> Such natural weapons delivered a potent venom that could render a victim [[Sleep/Legends|unconscious]] for several [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]].<ref name="GATORW" /><ref name="TOTRC" /> Not even Koboks were immune to such effects; it was possible for careless individuals to knock themselves out.<ref name="G DB" /> Koboks possessed four-fingered hands and three-toed feet.<ref name="GATORW" /> Members of the species walked with the torso angled slightly forward.<ref name="TRG" />

Each Kobok possessed three compound [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] set into spiked sockets<ref name="GATORW" /> and covered by lids. Although the carapace was tough and [[Chitin/Legends|chitinous]] like that of many insectoid species, their spiky brows could move to create expressions.<ref name="TRG" /> Two of these organs were positioned at the front of the head roughly where a [[Human/Legends|Human's]] eyes were located, and one was at the center of the back of the head.<ref name="G DB" /><ref name="SWE" /> Each eye had a wide field of vision,<ref name="RFF">''[[Rebel Force: Firefight]]''</ref> so in tandem, the three visual organs provided the Kobok with a 360-degree view of his or her surroundings. These visual organs were red or orange in color.<ref name="GATORW" /><ref name="G DB" /> Although the Kobok mouth featured insectoid mandibles, it opened to reveal a humanoid interior, including sharp, white [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]<ref name="TOTRC" /> and a red tongue. This physiology allowed the Kobok to create humanoid facial expressions, such as a smile.<ref name="TRG" /> Two small, flat nostrils perforated the front of the face.<ref name="GATORW" /> Koboks were covered in a thin fuzz, and they were able to grow the hair on their faces long,<ref name="SWE" /> with some individuals even gathering their facial fuzz into a sort of ponytail beard.<ref name="TRG" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:GaffR2-TofRC.png|thumb|right|270px|Koboks were reputed to be aggressive and violent by members of other species.]]
The Koboks hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Koboth, where they were governed by the united body of the [[Koboth Union]]. A history of violence and warfare, coupled with the harsh and unforgiving nature of their homeworld, made the Koboks a hardy and calculating species. This temperament made them particularly suited for [[Soldier/Legends|military]] and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] work. Non-Koboks in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large saw them as crafty [[Death/Legends|killing]] machines, a perception only solidified by the Koboks' proclivity for violent professions.<ref name="GATORW" />

The elite of the Kobok military was known as the [[Kobothi S-Corps]], a body that had been created less than a decade before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The S-Corps was charged with protecting Kobothi [[Realspace/Legends|space]] and interests. The organization used its own [[Unidentified Kobothi S-Corps "code" languages|"code" languages]], known only to members of the unit.<ref name="GATORW" /> The species had access to standard galactic technology, although some Koboks modified their [[Starship/Legends|starships]] to take advantage of their 360-degree field of vision; for example, a Kobok might place radar screens directly behind the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]].<ref name="RFF" /> The species spread to the surrounding [[Star system/Legends|systems]] and engaged in trade with their galactic neighbors, such as the [[Trianii/Legends|Trianii]] and the [[Hiitian/Legends|Hiitian]] species. They also came into frequent conflict with the power-hungry [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]], as their territories bordered one another.<ref name="GATORW" />

The species spoke and wrote [[Kobothi]], their native [[Language/Legends|language]], which was composed of tonal hisses.<ref name="GATORW" /> The word ''chsthiss'' was a farewell greeting in Kobothi.<ref name="RFF" /> Kobothi was difficult to translate into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], although the Koboks were able to speak that language as well. Examples of Kobok names included Kasj, Koas, Slis, and Tiska. Koboks wore very little clothing other than small scraps of cloth or [[Leather/Legends|leather]] straps.<ref name="GATORW" />

==History==
[[File:Kobothi_insurgency_mantle.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The Koboth Insurgent Mantle was a blue cape typically worn by veterans of the Mavvan Conflict.]]
The Koboks evolved on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] planet of Koboth, on the border of the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]]. As they spread across the six continents and numerous island chains of their homeworld, a planet scorched by [[Star/Legends|solar]] flares, they diverged into several races distinguished by the color of their carapaces. Although the Koboks had no contact with the greater [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] for millennia, they developed [[Hyperspace/Legends|sub-light]] space travel on their own. The species spread to surrounding systems and established a sphere of influence known as [[Kobothi Space]]. Over thousands of years, they warred constantly with one another. However, with the rise of the Koboth Union several centuries before the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Koboks were united under a single government and began to encounter other sentient species.<ref name="GATORW" />

Although they never joined the Old Republic, the Koboks brokered trade agreements with both the Trianii and the Hiitians centuries before the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] and [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Scout/Legends|explorers]] eventually came across the Koboks and found the insectoids already engaged in intra-system flight. These contacts resulted in the blazing of [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]] to Kobothi Space and brought the planet Koboth into contact with the greater galaxy via the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] hyperlane.<ref name="GATORW" />

Because of their proximity to the Corporate Alliance and its planetary holdings, the Koboks became engaged in territorial disputes with their neighbor. One such altercation erupted around [[10 BBY/Legends|10 BBY]], a dispute that turned more violent than past conflicts. This caused the Koboks to increase the degree of militarization in their society to become even more combat-ready. The Koboks became heavily involved in what became known as the [[Mavvan Conflict]], which in turn led to the creation of the Kobothi S-Corps. Those Koboks who earned distinction in these conflicts were awarded the [[Koboth Insurgent Mantle]],<ref name="GATORW" /> a blue cape.<ref name="TOTRC" /> The events further defined the Koboks' galaxy-wide image as capable soldiers.<ref name="GATORW" />

==Koboks in the galaxy==
===A warrior race===
After their homeworld was opened to trade, some Koboks spread across the galaxy, working as soldiers and mercenaries. Outside Kobothi Space, however, they remained fairly rare. Due to their martial prowess and warrior-like nature, Koboks quickly became associated with mercenary and [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] work. Although they were not a malicious species, these assignments earned them a reputation for being vicious, not unlike another species, the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]]. Some [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-using]] Koboks were known, but these were exceedingly rare. Other Koboks found work as scouts.<ref name="GATORW" />

The planet [[Roon/Legends|Roon]] was a destination for many Koboks who traveled offworld. When the population of Roon had reached 665,000, Koboks made up three percent of the populace. Koboks raised away from their homeworld, such as those on Roon, often were raised to speak Basic rather than Kobothi.<ref name="GATORW" />

===Gaff and Dualli===
{{Quote|I must say, Master Mungo, it's a little late now to realize the error of your ways!''"<br />"''Don't worry; he'll have plenty of time to regret it!|C-3PO and Gaff discuss Mungo Baobab's fate|<ref name="TFC" />}}
[[File:Droids-trailroon.jpg|thumb|right|280px|The Kobok Gaff considered his service to Governor Koong of Roon to be the low point of his career.]]
A notable Roon-born Kobok was the mercenary and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] collaborator, [[Gaff]]. At some point, Gaff visited his species' homeworld and joined the Kobothi S-Corp, but during the reign of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], he returned to Roon. He often wore a Koboth Insurgent Mantle, although it was not known if he actually participated in the Mavvan Conflict. After his return to Roon, Gaff allied himself with [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Bisad Koong|Koong]], an employment he considered the nadir of his career. During his work for Koong, at a [[Time/Legends|time]] which he was referred to by some as the governor's "henchman,"<ref name="GATORW" /> he came into conflict with the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Mungo Baobab]] and his [[Droid/Legends|droids]], [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. Gaff assaulted and captured them on several occasions, but the Human and his droids ultimately escaped and defeated Gaff in each instance.<ref name="TOTRC" /><ref name="TFC" /><ref name="TRG" /><ref name="ATRS">{{DroidsCite|Across the Roon Sea}}</ref> Gaff was thought to have escaped Roon after Koong's demise, likely fleeing along the Roon&ndash;[[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] corridor to search for new employment.<ref name="GATORW" />

[[Slis Tieeer Dualli]] was a yellow-hued Kobok mercenary.<ref name="RFF" /> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates ''[[Rebel Force: Firefight]]'' to [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> he was a veteran of more than twenty years of mercenary activity, having taken jobs [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]], assassinating targets, and flying. He considered himself the greatest Kobok pilot in the galaxy&mdash;and the greatest pilot of any species in the Outer Rim. Dualli had a temper, though; if a boss crossed him, the Kobok's impulse was to kill the employer. Such disloyalty earned Dualli a reputation as a loose cannon and made jobs hard for him to secure by 0 ABY. That year, Dualli was hired along with nine other top-tier pilots by an anonymous party&mdash;unbeknownst to them, a Human assassin known as [[X-7]]. Dualli and the others flew to [[Iope]], the third moon of [[Rinn/Legends|Rinn]], with vague promises of a huge payout if they accomplished their mission. However, once Dualli and his compatriots arrived, their employer began firing on them in an attempt to weed out the best among them. Dualli was killed in the [[Skirmish on Iope|skirmish]].<ref name="RFF" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Gaff_prototype_cutout.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kenner's preliminary sketch of the Kobok Gaff showed him with purple skin and yellow eyes.]]
Koboks were created for "[[Tail of the Roon Comets]],"<ref name="TOTRC" /> the tenth episode of the [[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO|''Star Wars: Droids'']] animated television series, which aired on [[November 9]], [[1985]].<ref name="SWCel">{{InsiderCite|27|A Star Wars CELibration|A ''Star Wars'' CELibration}}</ref>

[[Kenner Products|Kenner]] intended to sell an action figure version of the Kobok character. The toy company created a cardboard-cutout sketch of a Gaff action figure as a placeholder until a prototype could be created; it gave the character a lavender carapace and yellow eyes. The sculpted prototype of the character corrected these errors to show the Kobok with the same color scheme as that which he sports in the ''Droids'' cartoon series. The [[Star Wars: Droids (toy line)|''Star Wars: Droids'' toy line]] was canceled before a Gaff toy could reach stores.<ref name="25YoC">{{SWArchive|url=vault/collecting/droids_ewoks_25th_anniversary/index.html|text=25 Years of Collecting ''Droids'' and ''Ewoks''!}}.</ref>
